model: A payload field takes its own explosion (terminal:explosion()), none (terminal:no_explosion()) or any option below as hd2.explosion(name).

An option is a catalogued explosion whose package is known: Runtime loads that package before the write (the operation waits, waiting_for_assets) or, for the mission effects package, needs none (resident in every mission). An objective's explosion (warning objective_packages: EXCESSIVELY LARGE NUKE, the Cyborg Production Unit's) loads both of its objective packages, effect and sound. A package that cannot be loaded within 90 s rejects the operation with ASSET_UNAVAILABLE and the row keeps its value.
An option's label may differ from the catalogue's (note says why); its name is the catalogue id.
Every option needs allow_unverified_reference and allow_unverified_effect (no catalogued payload is live-tested), plus the field's own acknowledgements (fields[].acknowledgements.catalogue).
A field refuses an option whose shrapnel chain releases the row it writes (fields[].excluded); the write path re-proves the chain live.
The option's explosion row is only referenced: its own values stay those of its owner, and editing them (hd2.explosion(name)) changes every owner.

warnings.very_large: A very large blast (2000 damage or more, or an outer radius of 20 m or more): it can kill the shooter and teammates nearby.
warnings.lingering_field: Leaves a lingering status field (gas, EMS, smoke...). The game holds at most 4096 of them and does not check the count: avoid it on fast-firing weapons.
warnings.shrapnel: Releases shrapnel or bomblets (projectiles of their own).
warnings.no_damage: Deals no damage itself (its effect is a status field, smoke or a push).
warnings.objective_packages: Loads two objective packages of about 300 MB before the write (up to 90 s, a hitch while they load); they stay loaded for the session.
